About this page

  • In this page we review the literature which document the development of Adela’s cfMeDIP-seq Technology. The source of all the information contained therein is public.


1 AI Reports

  • AI reports are produced by claude.ai Opus 4.5 with naive prompts from Francois Collin.

  • The reporting done is intended to provide the information needed to underestand the roots and development of Adela’s cfMeDIP-seq Technology.


1.1 Adela vs GRAIL

  • A fairly comprehensive, high level comparison of the two platforms.

  • This compilation is for background purposes - see the documentation below for comments on technical aspects of some of the studies cited.


1.2 cfMeDIP-seq: Protocol, Pipeline and Classifiers

  • The evolution of Adela’s cfMeDIP-seq Protocol, Pipeline and Classifiers is traced.
  • The report is a fairly comprehensive, high level description of the assay and algorithm along with a description of enhancements that followed.


1.3 Differential Methylation Analysis Methodology

  • Survey DMA methods used with each assay type
  • Describe the analyis data in each step
  • Survey of benchmarking studies and tools


1.4 Enrichment-Based Differential Methylation Analysis

  • For enrichment-Based assays, a look at Bioinformatics Pipelines and Statistical Methods for Differential Methylation Analysis:
    • Common Bioinformatics Pipeline:FASTQ->BAN
    • DMA Methods for Enrichment based assays


1.4.1 RF vs elastic net: does RF edge enet and why?

  • From personal experience enet should do better with RF performance dropping substantially in the validation/evaliation set.
  • Also from Statistical learning with big data. A talk by Trevor Hastie (University of Bristol):
    • wide data - many features but few observations - calls for special methods to avoid overfitting. The elastic net is one of those methods.
    • tall data - many observations but reasonable number of features - not at risk of overfitting and can fit richer models with high orders of interactions.
